description: Texas payroll figures for 2026. Texas has no state personal income tax; employers pay unemployment insurance (UI) tax to the Texas Workforce Commission.

sources.title: Texas Workforce Commission, Your 2026 Tax Rates
sources.revision: page text captured 2026-09-29 and supplied 2026-09-30 (no revision date shown)

incomeTaxWithholding.note: Texas has no state personal income tax.

effectiveRate.note: The effective rate is the sum of five components. The employer's own effective rate comes from its TWC rate notice (entered in Payroll > Setup); these components explain it and are not used to compute it.

generalTaxRate.note: Benefit ratio (chargebacks / taxable wages, Q4 2022 through Q3 2025 for 2026) times the replenishment ratio; 0.00% with no chargebacks.

effectiveRate.check: Minimum 0.32% = GTR 0.00 + RTR 0.21 + OA 0.00 + interest 0.01 + DTR 0.00 + ETIA 0.10.

unemployment.newEmployerRateNote: The supplied page does not state the new-employer rate. Until it is sourced, a new Texas employer must enter the rate from its TWC notice.

cite.ref: "You pay unemployment tax on the first $9,000 that each employee earns during the calendar year."
"The minimum tax rate for 2026 is 0.32 percent. The maximum tax rate for 2026 is 6.32 percent."
Components: replenishment ratio 1.20%; RTR 0.21% (reduced by 0.10% to offset the ETIA); no Bond Obligation Assessment Rate for 2026; Interest Tax Rate 0.01%; no Deficit Tax Rate for 2026; ETIA 0.10%
